paper.title: Expert with Clustering: Hierarchical Online Preference Learning Framework

settings.name_in_paper: Online preference learning cast as prediction with expert advice (cluster centroids as experts), N users, T rounds per user
unmapped: N users each run a separate Hedge instance over K cluster-centroid experts; the user's choice y_{i,t} is revealed so all expert losses are observed
user preference parameters theta_i drawn from a distribution P with finite kurtosis; centroids learned from offline training data via (k-Means) clustering
regret measured against the oracle prediction using each user's true theta_i rather than the best expert
settings.definition_quote: We define the regret of EWC as the performance difference between EWC and Oracle $\boldsymbol{\theta}_{i}$: R_{EWC} = \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{t=1}^T ( \langle \mathbf{p}_{i,t}, \mathbf{l}_{i,t}\rangle - | \hat{y}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_i, x_{i,t})-y_{i,t}|^2 )

symbols.sigma_P_sq: variance of the preference distribution P, E_P||theta_i - mu||^2
symbols.E_Lclust: expected total squared clustering distance E_P[sum_i ||c_{k*(i)} - theta_i||^2]

conditions: theta_i drawn from distribution P with finite kurtosis
yhat(., x_i) Lipschitz with constant L under L2 distance and dimension normalization
offline sample size m >= 12800(8+M4)/(eps^2 delta) (3 + 30K(d+4) log 6K + log(1/delta)) (k-Means uniform deviation bound)
tuning: Hedge learning rate tuned for 2 sqrt(T log K) regret

source.label: EWC_Bound
source.quote: If $\mathbf{\hat{y}}(\cdot, \mathbf{x}_i)$ is Lipschitz continuous for all $\mathbf{x}_i$ with Lipschitz constant $L$, L$_2$ norm distance, and dimension normalization, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of EWC is bounded by: R_{EWC}\leq \overline{R}_{EWC}=2N\sqrt{T\log K} +  TL\left(\frac{\epsilon}{2}\sigma^2+(\frac{\epsilon}{2}+1)\mathbb{E}_P[\mathcal{L}]\right)

results.notes: Theorem number inferred from \newtheorem{EWC}{Theorem}[section] in Section 4; the paper does not print it. The paper's K (number of clusters/experts) is mapped to N_exp. The regret is measured against the oracle theta_i predictor, which does not fit the comparator vocabulary well. The probability is over the k-Means deviation bound.

symbols.l_centroids: L*eps/(2N)*sigma^2 + L*(eps/2+1)*sum_k pi_k trace(Sigma_k), the average loss caused by centroids

conditions: P is a Gaussian mixture with K components (weights pi_k, means mu_k, covariances Sigma_k)
clustering outputs the optimal centroids c_k = mu_k

source.label: EWC_Bound_GMM
source.quote: If $P$ is a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) with K Gaussian distributions, each of which has weight $\pi_k$, mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_k$, and covariance $\Sigma_k$, and the clustering outputs the optimal centroids where $\mathbf{c}_{k}=\boldsymbol{\mu}_k$. ... With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of EWC is bounded by R_{EWC}\leq \overline{R}_{EWC}= 2N\sqrt{T\log K} +  TNl_{centroids}

results.notes: Corollary number inferred from the counter definition and not printed by the paper.
